finding.claim: Path traversal / arbitrary file read in /dl. The user-supplied name is joined to the root with filepath.Join, which only cleans the path and does not confine it. Input such as ../../etc/passwd resolves outside /srv/files and the file contents are returned. The endpoint has no authentication.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter 'f' on GET /dl (files.go:12), fully attacker-controlled and unauthenticated
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: name := r.URL.Query().Get("f") takes raw user input with no validation
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to /etc/passwd, so the root prefix is escaped
w.Write(data) returns the file contents to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No prefix check after Join, no filepath.Base, no os.Root or fs.ValidPath, no auth middleware, no symlink check. The /avatar handler (files.go:22) does use filepath.Base and is not vulnerable, so the control is missing only in /dl.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 pass the raw query param f into filepath.Join(root, name) with no containment check, so ../../etc/passwd resolves to /etc/passwd, and files.go:18 writes it out on the unauthenticated /dl route (files.go:32); only /avatar (files.go:22) uses filepath.Base.

verdict_facts.reason: files.go:12-13 pass the raw query param 'f' into filepath.Join(root, name) with no containment check, so "../../etc/passwd" resolves to /etc/passwd and files.go:18 writes it to the response, with no auth on /dl (files.go:32); only /avatar uses filepath.Base (files.go:22).
